title: GDScript RPC Call Fails due to Typing
body:
### Tested versions

4.2.2
4.3

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.22631 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated GeForce GTX 1070 - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8700K CPU @ 3.70GHz (12 Threads)

### Issue description

Godot errors when an argument of an Array of a custom class is passed in to a function that has typing for the exact same type of array. This might be similar to error #53847.

This bug is definitely preventable user-side (that's me!), but it's pretty obscure and annoying to detect. I'm not very experienced at programming, so please let me know if there's some way I can improve!

Here is the error message:
E 0:00:04:0621   _process_rpc: RPC - 'Node(lobby.gd)::startingHand': Cannot convert argument 1 from Array to Array
  <C++ Source>   modules/multiplayer/scene_rpc_interface.cpp:290 @ _process_rpc()

### Steps to reproduce

Requirements for error:

- RPC call on a peer (not the host)
- Function has typing for a custom object (I have not tried stuff like integers, there is a chance that the same issue occurs there as well)
- VariableToPassIn is typed OR not typed
- When passing the variable into the function, do NOT put "as Array[x]"


My code is as follows (can be found in the scripts\autoload\lobby.gd https://github.com/WywySenarios/Senarios/commit/d3367df815b115a86a50e719c6f41c9d32335968)
```gdscript
## starts the game
@rpc("authority", "reliable", "call_local")
func startGame():
	# load the correct scene
	get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://scenes/level.tscn")

	
	if multiplayer.is_server():
		# the server is responsible for telling the users which starting hands they have received
		for i in players:
			# shuffle everyones' decks without notifying them
			players[i].deck.shuffle()
			
			# tell the player which starting hand they have received
			var cardsToPassIn: Array[Card] = [players[i].deck.content[0], players[i].deck.content[1], players[i].deck.content[2], players[i].deck.content[3]]
			startingHand.rpc_id(i, cardsToPassIn)
```

```gdscript
## Called by the server to notify the client about their starting hand.
@rpc("authority", "call_local", "reliable")
func startingHand(cards: Array[Card]):
	for i in range(len(cards)):
		print("emits", i, cards[i])
		newCard.emit(i, cards[i])
```

This is strange because the typing is *exactly* the same. This bug does not appear when calling on the host (id = 1), but it does appear when it is called on a peer (id != 1). This bug also appears if I define the type of cardsToPassIn above the for loop, and it also occurs if I define cardsToPassIn as [Card.new(), Card.new(), Card.new(), Card.new()]
I'm not experienced in coding, but I don't think this should be happening.

The error does not appear when I call:

```gdscript
startingHand.rpc_id(i, cardsToPassIn as Array[Card])
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[typecastingmrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18262054/typecastingmrp.zip)

Run two instances of the project.

Press the HOST button on the first window, then press the PEER button the second window, then press START button the first window. You'll see the error pop up in the debug menu.
